raw_answer_text:
Looking at the errors: node declarations (`process`, `decision`, `terminator`) parsed fine — only the bare `id -> id` edge lines failed. In this genre, edge lines need their own leading keyword, just like node lines do. I'm applying the minimal, evidence-based fix: prefix each edge with `edge`, without touching anything the validator didn't flag (including the honest `# GAP` comment and the class-based substitute for the requested border, since flowchart's own container construct was withdrawn and there is no other way to draw a literal box around a node subset in this genre).

```fd
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "Change request procedure"

# GAP: the flowchart genre withdrew "group" (its bordered-container
# construct); there is no remaining way in this genre to draw
# a literal border around a subset of nodes. Composed substitute instead: a
# shared class marks the two steps that fall inside the scheduled
# maintenance window, and its meaning text carries that claim through the
# legend. This is NOT a bordered box — flag this to the reader, it is an
# approximation, not the requested enclosure.
class window "Falls within the scheduled change window" stroke=#2563eb

process receive "Receive change request"
process validate "Validate against policy" class=window
decision isvalid "Valid?"
process apply "Apply change to device" class=window
terminator confirm "Confirm success"
terminator rollback "Roll back"

edge receive -> validate
edge validate -> isvalid
edge isvalid -> apply "yes"
edge isvalid -> rollback "no"
edge apply -> confirm
```

Note for the next repair round if `edge` is still rejected: the only signal I have from this run is that bare `id -> id` lines are not a recognized line start in `flowchart`, so a leading keyword is required — I chose `edge` as the generic term the top-level doc itself uses for this construct across genres ("a node, an edge, a field, a row..."). If the validator names a different required spelling, that error message is authoritative over this guess and should be applied verbatim, per "read the error instead of guessing around it."
